program.title: AI Engineer Program
program.blurb: Go from Python basics to shipping production RAG and multi-agent systems, using only free resources.
program.credit: 5-step roadmap adapted from the "Zero-to-Hired AI Engineer Roadmap 2026" by Satya Explains. 100-day plan from your own sheet.

why.intro: An AI engineer is a software engineer who builds applications on top of pre-trained AI models, using LLM APIs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agent frameworks. The job is about applying models well, not inventing new ones, so strong software skills matter more than a maths PhD.

stats.label: AI Engineer was LinkedIn's fastest-growing job title in the US for two years running (Jobs on the Rise 2026)
Wage premium for roles that require AI skills, up from 25% the year before (PwC Global AI Jobs Barometer 2025)
Indicative India salary range, entry to senior (LPA). Entry 8-12, mid 18-30, senior 35-60+. Pay varies a lot by company and city.

why.note: Figures are as reported in the source roadmap and are indicative only.

steps.title: Python
steps.tagline: The main language of AI. Learn it by building, not just watching.
steps.outcome: Write real programs, not just follow tutorials.
todo: Watching tutorials is fine, but the real learning happens when you build projects.
Follow the 30 Days of Python repo. Each day has explanations, exercises and small projects.
Cover the basics (variables, data types, loops, functions), then files, APIs, classes and pandas.
Goal: write and debug a small program on your own, without copy-pasting.

steps.title: Core Concepts
steps.tagline: Learn the basics first. Go deeper later.
steps.outcome: Math, statistics and ML basics - enough to build.
todo: Math: build intuition for linear algebra, calculus and how neural networks learn.
Statistics: probability, distributions, bias vs variance, how to judge a model.
ML concepts: supervised vs unsupervised learning, regression, classification, evaluation.
You do not need to master everything. Learn enough to build, then return when a project demands more.

resources.label: 3Blue1Brown
resources.note: Visual maths: linear algebra, calculus, neural networks

resources.label: Andrew Ng - Stanford CS229 (full lecture playlist)

steps.title: Under the Hood
steps.tagline: Where most people go wrong: jumping straight to frameworks.
steps.outcome: Understand what happens inside a GPT-style model.
todo: Before reaching for any framework, build a GPT from scratch with Andrej Karpathy.
In about two hours you code a small character-level GPT and see attention and transformers in action.
After this you will know what is really happening inside the model, which makes every later step easier.

resources.label: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
resources.note: Full series on Andrej Karpathy's channel

steps.title: AI Systems
steps.tagline: Everything around the model is what makes it a product.
steps.outcome: Evals, caching, RAG, tools and MCP.
todo: Learn the building blocks of real AI systems: inference, evals, caching, pipelines, embeddings, vector databases, tool calling and MCP.
Then pick up production tools such as LangChain and LangGraph.

resources.label: LangChain documentation
resources.note: Framework for LLM apps, agents and RAG

resources.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
resources.note: Standard way to connect models to tools and data

resources.label: Hugging Face
resources.note: Pre-trained models, datasets and deployment tools

steps.title: Build
steps.tagline: Get your hands dirty. This is what separates a demo from a real project.
steps.outcome: A production RAG app and a multi-agent system, with evals and observability.
todo: Build a production-style RAG app: ingest documents, chunk, embed, store in a vector database, retrieve and answer with sources.
Build a multi-agent system: agents with different roles that call tools and hand work to each other.
Add evals to both: a test set, scoring and regression checks, so you know when a change makes things worse.
Add observability to both: trace every call, track latency, cost and failures.
Deploy at least one project with a live link and write a short README explaining your design choices.

resources.label: LangSmith
resources.note: Tracing and evals - observe and evaluate LLM apps

checklist: RAG app with sources, deployed with a live link
Multi-agent system that uses at least two tools
Eval set and scores for both projects
Tracing and observability dashboards for both
GitHub README for each project: problem, design, results
mistakes: Spending months on theory before writing any code.
Jumping into frameworks without understanding what a model actually does.
Paying for expensive bootcamps or collecting certificates instead of shipping projects.
Stopping at a demo. Add evals and observability so it behaves like a real product.
